title: Capital Gains Tax on Shares: How to Calculate It
excerpt: Capital gains tax on shares is calculated by working out the capital gain from the sale of shares and then determining the taxable capital gain.
content:
Capital gains tax on shares is calculated by working out the capital gain from the sale of shares and then determining the taxable capital gain. When you calculate capital gains tax on shares, you need to consider the selling price, cost base, allowable costs, capital losses, and the length of time the shares have been held.

For example, when you calculate capital gains tax on shares, you first need to work out the capital gain from the sale of the shares. The amount left after subtracting the cost base and allowable expenses from the selling price is your capital gain. This calculation is used when working out shares and capital gains tax, share gain tax, and capital gains in stocks.

Capital Gains Tax on Inherited Shares

When you calculate capital gains tax on inherited shares, you need to work out the capital gain from the sale of the shares. To calculate the capital gain, subtract the cost base of the shares from the selling price. The amount left after this calculation is your capital gain.

How Do I Calculate Capital Gains Tax on Shares?

To calculate capital gains tax on shares, use the following calculation:

Capital Gain = Selling Price − Cost Base − Allowable Expenses

The costs related to purchasing, owning and selling the asset can be considered when working out the gain from the sale. This calculation can be used when you calculate capital gains tax on shares or work out capital gains from shares sale.

How to Work Out Capital Gains Tax on Shares

When you work out capital gains tax on shares, you need to consider the selling price, cost base, allowable expenses, capital losses, and applicable CGT discount.

You also need to know whether you are eligible for a capital gains tax discount. If an individual holds an asset for more than 12 months, they may receive a 50% CGT discount. After applying the applicable discount, the remaining capital gain is used to determine how much tax you may need to pay.

The capital gain is added to your taxable income before the applicable tax is calculated. Select the income year in which you received the income when using the capital gains tax calculator.

CGT Discount on Shares

Individuals and trusts can receive a 50% CGT discount if they hold an asset for more than 12 months. Companies are generally not eligible for the 50% CGT discount.

After applying the applicable discount to your capital gain, the remaining capital gain is used to determine how much tax you may need to pay.

Capital Losses on Shares

If you have any capital losses from previous years, you can subtract them from your current capital gains before calculating CGT. This can reduce your taxable capital gain and the amount of Capital Gains Tax you need to pay.
